blocks.text: After the Mauryas, the north-west saw a succession of foreign powers — **Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians and Kushans**. The **Kushans**, peaking under **Kanishka**, built a **Central-Asia-to-Ganga empire**, championed **Mahayana Buddhism and Gandhara-Mathura art**, and controlled the **Silk Route**.

rows: First to issue **gold coins** & **coins with king's portraits**; **Menander (Milinda)** — Buddhist (Milindapanho with Nagasena); introduced **Hellenistic (Gandhara) art**.
**Rudradaman I** — Junagadh inscription (first long Sanskrit inscription); repaired Sudarshana lake; Saka era.
**Kanishka (c. 78 CE)** — greatest; started the **Saka Era (78 CE)**; capital **Purushapura (Peshawar)** & Mathura.
**4th Buddhist Council (Kashmir)** → Mahayana; patronised **Ashvaghosha, Nagarjuna, Charaka, Vasumitra**.
Realistic Buddha, wavy hair, thick drapery

blocks.text: The **Satavahanas (c. 1st BCE–3rd CE)** were the **first major Deccan power** after the Mauryas, ruling from **Pratishthana (Paithan)**. They revived **Brahmanism, patronised Buddhism (Amaravati), promoted maritime (Roman) trade**, and issued **lead & potin coins** — bridging north and south India.

rows: Founder **Simuka**; greatest **Gautamiputra Satakarni** (defeated the Shakas — Nasik prashasti of **Gautami Balasri**).
**Matronymic** names (Gautamiputra, Vasishthiputra); feudal 'ratika/maharathi' chiefs; **land grants to Brahmins/monks (first)**.
Flourishing **Roman trade** (ports, coins); guilds (shreni); **lead, potin, copper coins**.
**Prakrit** official language; **Hala's Gathasaptashati**; **Amaravati stupa** art; caves at Nasik, Karle.

items: **Satavahanas / Andhras (1st c BCE – 3rd c CE)**, capital **Pratishthana (Paithan)** on Godavari; founder **Simuka**; greatest **Gautamiputra Satakarni** (defeated Shakas/Nahapana — restruck his coins; **Nasik prashasti** by mother **Gautami Balashri**); **Vashishtiputra Pulumavi**.

**Polity & society**: **matronymics** (kings named after mothers — Gautamiputra, Vashishtiputra) though **patriarchal**; brahmanical revival + Buddhist patronage; earliest **land grants (to Brahmins & monks, tax-free)** in India.
**Economy**: brisk **Roman trade** (Periplus, Ptolemy); ports; **lead, copper, potin coins** (also silver); guilds (shreni) & **nigama**.
**Language & art**: **Prakrit** (official), **Gathasaptasati** by **Hala**; **Amaravati & Nagarjunakonda** stupas (white-marble narrative art); **Karle, Bhaja, Nasik** rock-cut chaityas/viharas.
**Significance**: bridged north & south; first great Deccan state; forerunner of Andhra's Ikshvakus.

sections.heading: The Sangam Age — society, literature & economy

blocks.text: The **Sangam Age (c. 300 BCE–300 CE)** was the classical era of the **Tamil south**, ruled by the **three crowned kings — Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas**. Its **Sangam literature** (Tamil academies at Madurai) is the primary source, revealing a **prosperous trade economy and a distinctive Tamil society**.

rows: **Chera (bow emblem, Vanji), Chola (tiger, Uraiyur/Kaveripattinam), Pandya (fish, Madurai)**.
Three Sangams (academies) at **Madurai** under Pandya patronage; most works from the **third Sangam**.
Rich **Roman trade** (Muziris port; Roman gold coins); pearls, spices, muslin; guilds.
Roman trade via **Arikamedu/Muziris** — gold & wine for pepper, pearls, muslin

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: the Sangam Age (far South)

**Three Sangams** (literary academies) at **Madurai** under Pandya patronage; the surviving corpus is the **Second/Third Sangam**.

**Literature (Tamil)**: **Tolkappiyam** (grammar, oldest), **Ettuthogai** (8 anthologies), **Pattuppattu** (10 idylls), **Pathinenkilkanakku** (18 minor works incl. **Tirukkural** by Thiruvalluvar); twin epics **Silappadikaram** (Ilango Adigal) & **Manimekalai** (Sattanar).

**Society & tinai**: five eco-zones — **Kurinji, Mullai, Marudam, Neydal, Palai**; classes Arasar/Anthanar/Vanigar/Vellalar; hero-stones (**nadukal**); position of women mixed (poets like **Avvaiyar**; but sati/widowhood).
**Economy**: flourishing **Indo-Roman trade** — **Arikamedu (Poduke), Muziris, Puhar**; exports pepper, pearls, muslin, spices; **Roman gold coins** hoards; guilds; Yavana (Roman) settlements.

blocks.text: The **Sunga dynasty (185–73 BCE)**, founded by **Pushyamitra Sunga** after assassinating the last Maurya, marked a **Brahmanical revival** and is famed for the **Bharhut and Sanchi stupa art** and the patronage of Sanskrit (Patanjali).

rows: **Pushyamitra Sunga** — a Maurya general who killed **Brihadratha (185 BCE)**; capital Pataliputra/Vidisha.
**Brahmanical revival**; performed **Ashvamedha** sacrifices; yet Buddhist art flourished.
**Bharhut & Sanchi stupa** railings/gateways (torana) enlarged; Heliodorus pillar (Besnagar).
Erected by a **Greek envoy (Heliodorus)** dedicated to **Vasudeva (Vishnu)** — early Bhagavatism.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: the Shungas & successors

**Brahmanical revival** but Buddhism continued — the **Bharhut & Sanchi stupa railings/toranas** and enlarged **Sanchi Stupa** belong to the Shunga era; **Patanjali** (Mahabhashya) associated with this court.

**Successors**: **Kanvas** (Vasudeva Kanva, 73 BCE) → then in the Deccan the **Satavahanas** rose; in Kalinga, **Kharavela (Cheta/Chedi dynasty)** — the **Hathigumpha inscription** (Udayagiri, Jain patron).
**Significance**: transition age of brahmanical resurgence, Sanskrit revival and classic early stupa art.

blocks.text: The **Gupta Empire (c. 319–550 CE)** ushered in a **'Classical/Golden Age'**. Founded by **Chandragupta I** and expanded by **Samudragupta and Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya)**, it featured a **decentralised administration, land-grant economy, revived Hinduism, and unmatched cultural achievement**.

rows: **Chandragupta I** (Gupta era 319-20 CE, Lichchhavi marriage), **Samudragupta** ('Napoleon of India' — Allahabad/Prayag Prashasti by **Harishena**), **Chandragupta II 'Vikramaditya'** (defeated Shakas; Fa-Hien visited; Navaratnas).
More **decentralised/feudal** than Mauryan; provinces (bhukti) → district (vishaya) → village; **land grants (agrahara)** rise.
Peak of **gold coins ('dinara')**; land revenue ~1/6; guilds; decline of long-distance trade later.
Rigid caste; **rise of untouchability & decline in women's status (early marriage, sati at Eran-510 CE)**.
Feudatory/Samanta system; Bhukti→Vishaya→village; lighter than Maurya

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Gupta administration, society, economy

items: **Dynasty**: **Sri Gupta → Chandragupta I** (Gupta era 319-20 CE; married Licchavi princess Kumaradevi; title Maharajadhiraja) → **Samudragupta** ('Indian Napoleon'; **Allahabad/Prayag Prashasti** by **Harishena** — digvijaya, Ashvamedha) → **Chandragupta II Vikramaditya** (defeated Western Shakas; **Fa-Hien** visited; Ujjain second capital; **Mehrauli iron pillar**) → Kumaragupta I (founded Nalanda) → Skandagupta (repelled Hunas).

**Administration**: **decentralised/feudal** — provinces (**Bhukti** under Uparika) → districts (**Vishaya** under Vishayapati) → **Vithi/village** (Gramika, record-keeper); rise of **Samanta** feudatories & **land grants (agrahara)** with fiscal/administrative rights → seeds of feudalism.

**Society**: **Brahmanical resurgence**; varna rigid; **untouchability** grew (Fa-Hien noted Chandalas outside towns); position of **women declined** (early marriage, first clear **sati** — Eran inscription 510 CE); but women held some property (stridhana).

**Economy**: gold **dinaras** (finest coins) but a shrinking silver economy later; **guilds (shreni)** issued their own seals; **decline of long-distance Roman trade**; land grants → localised, agrarian economy; **Fa-Hien** reports a prosperous, mild, cashless-in-parts polity.
**Religion**: **Bhagavatism/Vaishnavism** patronised (Garuda emblem); tolerance to Buddhism/Jainism; the **Puranas** compiled.
Samudragupta = Prayag Prashasti (Harishena); Chandragupta II = Vikramaditya, Fa-Hien, Navaratnas.
Gold coins peak, feudal land-grants, first sati inscription (Eran 510) — society/economy markers.

sections.heading: Gupta art, architecture, literature, science & technology

blocks.text: The Gupta age was the **classical peak of Indian culture** — the **first structural Hindu temples (Nagara), the Ajanta murals, Sanskrit literature (Kalidasa), and pioneering science (Aryabhata) and metallurgy (the rustless Iron Pillar)**.

rows: **First structural temples** — **Dashavatara temple (Deogarh), Bhitargaon (brick)**; **Nagara** style begins; **Nalanda University** (Kumaragupta).
**Aryabhata** (Aryabhatiya — zero-place value, earth's rotation, π); **Varahamihira (Brihatsamhita)**; **Brahmagupta**; **Sushruta/Charaka** medicine.
**Mehrauli Iron Pillar** — rust-free; advanced iron technology.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Gupta 'Golden Age' — art, letters, science

items: **Literature**: **Kalidasa** (Abhijnana-Shakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Malavikagnimitra); **Vishakhadatta** (Mudrarakshasa, Devichandraguptam); **Shudraka** (Mrichchhakatika); **Vishnu Sharma** (Panchatantra); **Amarasimha** (Amarakosha); Puranas & Smritis (Narada, Yajnavalkya) finalised.

**Science & mathematics**: **Aryabhata** (Aryabhatiya — **zero, decimal place value, value of π, earth's rotation, eclipse causes**); **Varahamihira** (Brihat Samhita, Panchasiddhantika); **Brahmagupta** (rules for zero/negatives); **Sushruta & Charaka Samhitas** (surgery/medicine); **Mehrauli iron pillar** (rust-resistant metallurgy).

**Art & architecture**: birth of the structural **Nagara temple** — **Dashavatara temple, Deogarh** & **Bhitargaon** (brick); **Ajanta** murals (Vakataka-Gupta age); **Sarnath school** Buddha (Dhammachakra image), **Sultanganj bronze Buddha**; **Udayagiri caves** (Varaha panel).

**Why 'Golden Age'** (and caveats): peak of Sanskrit, classical arts, science, gold coinage & political stability — but it was **elite, Brahmanical, feudalising**, with declining women's status and trade.

blocks.text: One fact per domain proves the 'Golden Age': **Kalidasa** (letters), **Aryabhata** (science), **Deogarh Nagara temple** (architecture), **Ajanta murals** (painting), **dinaras** (economy).
